prompts.text: Re-fold GRUCellBlock so a companion feature front end can route beside it on one 10x12 chip, then finish the gru_classifier example. The gate that matters is co-placement of the GRU with the real RMS arm (ComplexToMagSquared -> MovingAverage(32) -> Sqrt -> KeepOneInN(32)) plus ZeroCrossingRate and FeaturePairJoin.

notes:
BLOCK-CLASS row (wave 7). The RE-FOLD SHIPPED AND IS VERIFIED; the example's co-placement wall did NOT fall, and the dispatch's stop-and-report clause was taken. Three results.

(1) THE RE-FOLD. GRUCellBlock now folds 8x7 (was 7x8) -- the same 50-cell closed serpentine, transposed, 51 cells unchanged. Chosen by exhaustive search over the comb / row-comb / spine-snake closed-cycle families x 8 D4 images x 100 start-and-direction pairs, filtered on every fold rule (closed cycle, <=8x8 per INV-9's D4 cap, no enclosed interior, the route-time face rule) and ranked by PORT COST -- min over anchors of |fin - x16_in| + |oout - x16_out|, which is the metric that matters because the 10x12's two 16-bit ports are BOTH on row 0. The old fold put the input on the north-west corner and buried the egress two rows down the WEST edge facing away from the output port: cost 11, with gru_out alone measuring 15-17 corridor cells. The transpose spans the NORTH edge (fin (0,0), oout (2,0)): cost 7, and it leaves five free ROWS rather than three free columns. All 53 block gates pass (52 pre-existing + the new INV-37 gate), including the 8-orientation D4 invariance. Behaviour is preserved EXACTLY, verified on the real chip after the re-fold: 36,000 on-chip steps at agreement 1.000000 against the golden, clip vote 0.9667 on-chip == 0.9667 offline over 120 held-out clips, and the mutation gates still fail correctly (weight corruption 37/40 -> 30/40; one-word h perturbation differs on 239/240 steps).

(2) THE REAL BUG THE RE-FOLD FOUND -- now INV-37, and the most transferable result here. The block baked THREE is_face=True constants as literals (fin's LOCK_FACE, amx's face_out and face_ring) matching the as-authored fold. Every re-fold attempted (a solid 5x10 Hamiltonian ring, the transpose, a reversed traversal of the same ring) produced a perfectly legal layout -- closed cycle, in-cap bbox, clean route-time face rule, correct dict ordering -- that BUILT and then computed garbage: 20 of 52 gates failed, the recurrence write-back never landed, h froze at its timestep-0 value, and whole-block simulation ran to EventLimit without completing. No geometric gate can see this because the geometry is correct. The constants are now DERIVED from the fold via a single _face_from(a, b) helper over the ring positions, with _ring_geometry() as the fold's single source of truth; the same transposed fold then passed all 52 gates unchanged. A new gate (test_every_baked_face_word_agrees_with_the_fold) asserts the three words against the placed geometry and was mutation-proven to FAIL on the old literals. Corollary worth remembering: a closed ring is direction-free for its @N hop distances but NOT for its faces -- reversing the traversal reverses every resting face.

(3) THE EXAMPLE WALL STANDS, AND BOTH NAMED LEVERS ARE NOW MEASURED NEGATIVE. The re-fold measurably HELPED: on the identical lane search the old 7x8 fold bottomed out TWO nets short and the 8x7 reaches ONE. It did not close it -- 4180 further layouts (exhaustive lane enumeration plus guided perturbation seeded from every one- and two-net-short result) stayed at exactly one net short, on join_gru / gru_out with reason 'no bus path from source to the broker tap'. Two structural findings explain why fold shape cannot be the lever: under INV-9's 8x8 cap a 51-cell block has only THREE possible bounding boxes (7x8, 8x7, 8x8), and a CLOSED RING can never contain a free through-channel (a cycle cannot jump a gap), so all its free space is perimeter -- free-space quality measured IDENTICAL (29 3x3-anchors, 48 2x2) across every legal fold, with only port proximity varying. The second named lever was swept too: shrinking the RMS arm across boxcar lengths 32/16/8/4 with and without Sqrt gives 65 block cells -> 4 nets short, 62 -> 2, 57 -> 1, 56 -> 1; even a 4-tap boxcar with Sqrt dropped (no longer the model's feature) is one net short.

THE MEASURED DIAGNOSIS, and the lever for whoever picks this up. The wall is the TEN NETS' CORRIDOR BUDGET, not cells and not fold shape: 65 block cells leave 55 for routing, the six-net join->GRU tail already costs 51 corridor cells (8.5/net, measured, routing at 81/120), so ten nets want ~85 and 65+85 = 150 > 120. The lever is therefore FEWER SEPARATELY PLACED BLOCKS, because that removes NETS as well as cells: one fused feature block computing the (rms, zcr) pair from (re, im) would absorb the six front-end blocks and delete SIX of the ten nets, estimating ~99/120 with real headroom. The fallback is a two-chip topology. Deliverables: the re-folded block + INV-37 + its gate, a new co-placement gate (test_coplacement_the_gru_leaves_room_for_the_companion_front_end) that asserts the whole block set places legally together and gets within one net -- and fails the day the last net closes -- the three known-limit guards updated to the new geometry, and the example's README/module prose carrying the measured numbers. No .kyt or .grc ships, because the chain still does not route as one chip.
